title: Pharmacology: Top 200 Drugs (generic)
description: For health-science learners: 200 commonly encountered US generic medicines, with class, a common use and a key caution. A study selection, not a ranked prescribing list or dosing guide; verify with current guidelines.

sources.name: DailyMed public prescribing-label database
sources.license: Public label reference; individual label rights vary; card wording original

sources.name: FDA: severe itching after stopping long-term cetirizine or levocetirizine

cards.back: Class: ACE inhibitor. Use: hypertension and selected heart-failure regimens. Key caution: angioedema and hyperkalemia; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: ACE inhibitor. Use: hypertension and heart failure. Key caution: renal dysfunction and hyperkalemia, especially with renal artery stenosis; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: ACE inhibitor. Use: hypertension and cardiovascular risk reduction in selected patients. Key caution: angioedema; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: angiotensin II receptor blocker. Use: hypertension and selected diabetic kidney disease. Key caution: hyperkalemia and fetal toxicity; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: angiotensin II receptor blocker. Use: hypertension and heart failure. Key caution: hyperkalemia and renal dysfunction; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: angiotensin II receptor blocker. Use: hypertension. Key caution: severe sprue-like enteropathy can occur; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: angiotensin II receptor blocker. Use: hypertension and diabetic nephropathy. Key caution: hyperkalemia and renal dysfunction; avoid in pregnancy.
Class: dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. Use: hypertension and angina. Key caution: dose-related peripheral edema.

Class: dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. Use: hypertension and angina with appropriate formulations. Key caution: hypotension; immediate-release formulations are not used for routine rapid blood-pressure reduction.
Class: non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. Use: rate control, hypertension and angina. Key caution: bradycardia and AV block; negative inotropy can worsen systolic heart failure.
Class: non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. Use: selected arrhythmias, hypertension and angina. Key caution: AV block and constipation; can worsen systolic heart failure.
Class: beta-1-selective blocker. Use: hypertension, angina and selected heart-failure treatment; formulation matters. Key caution: bradycardia; abrupt withdrawal can worsen ischemia.
Class: beta-1-selective blocker. Use: hypertension and angina. Key caution: bradycardia and accumulation with renal impairment.
Class: beta blocker with alpha-1 blockade. Use: heart failure and hypertension. Key caution: bradycardia, orthostatic hypotension and bronchospasm in susceptible patients.
Class: nonselective beta blocker. Use: tremor, migraine prevention and selected cardiovascular conditions. Key caution: bronchospasm; may mask adrenergic signs of hypoglycemia.
Class: beta blocker with alpha-1 blockade. Use: hypertension. Key caution: bradycardia and bronchospasm; rare serious liver injury.
Class: beta-1-selective blocker. Use: hypertension and selected heart-failure regimens. Key caution: bradycardia and worsening conduction block.
Class: thiazide diuretic. Use: hypertension and edema. Key caution: hyponatremia, hypokalemia and increased uric acid.
Class: thiazide-like diuretic. Use: hypertension. Key caution: electrolyte depletion, including hyponatremia and hypokalemia.
Class: loop diuretic. Use: edema from heart, kidney or liver disease. Key caution: volume depletion and hypokalemia; ototoxicity with high exposures.
Class: loop diuretic. Use: edema and hypertension. Key caution: dehydration and electrolyte depletion.
Class: loop diuretic. Use: edema. Key caution: potent fluid and electrolyte loss.
Class: mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist. Use: heart failure, resistant hypertension and hyperaldosteronism. Key caution: hyperkalemia; gynecomastia can occur.
Class: selective mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist. Use: selected heart failure and hypertension. Key caution: hyperkalemia and important CYP3A drug interactions.
Class: central alpha-2 agonist. Use: hypertension; some formulations treat ADHD. Key caution: abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound hypertension.
Class: direct arteriolar vasodilator. Use: hypertension and selected heart-failure combinations. Key caution: reflex tachycardia and drug-induced lupus.
Class: organic nitrate vasodilator. Use: angina and selected acute cardiovascular settings. Key caution: profound hypotension with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.
Class: long-acting nitrate. Use: prevention of angina. Key caution: hypotension and tolerance; not for immediate relief of an acute attack.
Class: cardiac glycoside. Use: selected heart failure and atrial-fibrillation rate control. Key caution: narrow therapeutic index; toxicity risk rises with renal impairment and hypokalemia.
Class: class III antiarrhythmic with multiple channel effects. Use: selected serious arrhythmias. Key caution: pulmonary, thyroid and hepatic toxicity, plus many interactions.
Class: class III antiarrhythmic and nonselective beta blocker. Use: selected atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. Key caution: QT prolongation and torsades; renal function affects exposure.
Class: class IC antiarrhythmic. Use: selected supraventricular arrhythmias. Key caution: proarrhythmia; generally avoided with ischemic or significant structural heart disease.
Class: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Use: LDL reduction and cardiovascular risk reduction. Key caution: muscle injury, especially with interacting medicines.
Class: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Use: LDL reduction and cardiovascular risk reduction. Key caution: myopathy; renal impairment affects dosing considerations.
Class: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Use: dyslipidemia. Key caution: myopathy risk increases with CYP3A inhibitors and certain other interacting drugs.
Class: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. Use: dyslipidemia and cardiovascular risk reduction. Key caution: myopathy and liver injury are possible.
Class: intestinal cholesterol-absorption inhibitor. Use: LDL reduction alone or with a statin. Key caution: liver-enzyme elevations are more likely when combined with a statin.
Class: fibrate; PPAR-alpha agonist. Use: severe hypertriglyceridemia and selected dyslipidemia. Key caution: renal impairment, gallstones and muscle toxicity.

Class: salicylate; irreversible cyclooxygenase inhibitor. Use: antiplatelet therapy in selected cardiovascular settings and pain or fever relief. Key caution: bleeding; avoid routine use for viral illness in children because of Reye syndrome risk.
Class: P2Y12 platelet inhibitor. Use: prevention of arterial thrombotic events. Key caution: bleeding; reduced CYP2C19 activation can reduce effectiveness.
Class: reversible P2Y12 platelet inhibitor. Use: selected acute coronary syndrome and secondary prevention regimens. Key caution: bleeding, dyspnea and significant drug interactions.

Class: vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant. Use: selected thromboembolic prevention and treatment, including mechanical valves. Key caution: major bleeding and many interactions; requires INR monitoring and can harm a fetus.
Class: direct factor Xa inhibitor. Use: selected atrial-fibrillation stroke prevention and venous thromboembolism. Key caution: bleeding; strong interacting drugs and patient factors affect use.
Class: direct factor Xa inhibitor. Use: selected atrial-fibrillation and venous thromboembolism indications. Key caution: bleeding; renal function and food requirements vary by regimen.
Class: direct thrombin inhibitor. Use: selected atrial-fibrillation and venous thromboembolism indications. Key caution: bleeding and renal accumulation; not for mechanical heart valves.
Class: low-molecular-weight heparin. Use: prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis and selected acute coronary syndromes. Key caution: bleeding, renal accumulation and neuraxial hematoma risk.
Class: indirect anticoagulant enhancing antithrombin activity. Use: acute anticoagulation in selected settings. Key caution: bleeding and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
Class: biguanide. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: rare lactic acidosis, especially with severe renal dysfunction or hypoxic illness; long-term use can lower vitamin B12.
Class: sulfonylurea insulin secretagogue. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: hypoglycemia and weight gain.
Class: sulfonylurea insulin secretagogue. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: hypoglycemia, particularly with reduced intake or impaired drug clearance.
Class: thiazolidinedione insulin sensitizer. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: fluid retention can cause or worsen heart failure; fracture risk may rise.
Class: DPP-4 inhibitor. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: pancreatitis has been reported; renal function affects dosing.
Class: DPP-4 inhibitor. Use: type 2 diabetes. Key caution: pancreatitis and severe joint pain have been reported.

Class: SGLT2 inhibitor. Use: type 2 diabetes and selected heart-failure or kidney-disease indications. Key caution: ketoacidosis can occur with only modest glucose elevation; genital infections and volume depletion.
Class: SGLT2 inhibitor. Use: type 2 diabetes and selected heart-failure or chronic-kidney-disease indications. Key caution: ketoacidosis, genital infections and dehydration.
Class: SGLT2 inhibitor. Use: type 2 diabetes and selected kidney and cardiovascular risk reduction. Key caution: ketoacidosis and volume depletion; monitor foot problems and amputation risk factors.

Class: GLP-1 receptor agonist. Use: type 2 diabetes or chronic weight management depending on formulation. Key caution: avoid with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; significant gastrointestinal effects.

Class: GLP-1 receptor agonist. Use: type 2 diabetes or chronic weight management depending on formulation. Key caution: medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 contraindication; pancreatitis is a warning.
Class: GLP-1 receptor agonist. Use: type 2 diabetes and selected cardiovascular risk reduction. Key caution: medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 contraindication; gastrointestinal intolerance.

Class: dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist. Use: type 2 diabetes or chronic weight management depending on product. Key caution: medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 contraindication; delayed gastric emptying can affect oral medications.
Class: long-acting basal insulin analog. Use: basal glucose control in diabetes. Key caution: hypoglycemia; not a substitute for rapid mealtime insulin.
Class: intermediate-acting human insulin suspension. Use: basal glucose control in diabetes. Key caution: a pronounced activity peak can cause hypoglycemia; suspension handling and timing matter.
Class: ultra-long-acting basal insulin analog. Use: basal glucose control in diabetes. Key caution: hypoglycemia and errors between different insulin concentrations.
Class: rapid-acting insulin analog. Use: mealtime glucose control. Key caution: hypoglycemia if insulin timing and carbohydrate intake do not match.
Class: rapid-acting insulin analog. Use: mealtime glucose control. Key caution: hypoglycemia and formulation-specific timing differences.
Class: short-acting human insulin. Use: glucose control; intravenous use in selected monitored settings. Key caution: hypoglycemia and potentially dangerous concentration mix-ups.
Class: synthetic thyroid hormone T4. Use: hypothyroidism. Key caution: excess replacement can cause arrhythmias and bone loss; absorption is reduced by iron and calcium.
Class: thionamide blocking thyroid hormone synthesis. Use: hyperthyroidism. Key caution: agranulocytosis and fetal risk, especially early in pregnancy.
Class: systemic glucocorticoid. Use: inflammatory and immune-mediated disorders. Key caution: infection, hyperglycemia and adrenal suppression with sustained exposure.
Class: systemic glucocorticoid. Use: inflammatory and allergic disorders. Key caution: infection risk and adrenal suppression with prolonged treatment.
Class: long-acting glucocorticoid. Use: selected inflammatory, oncologic and edema-related conditions. Key caution: hyperglycemia, infection and adrenal suppression.

Class: glucocorticoid with mineralocorticoid activity. Use: adrenal replacement or inflammation depending on formulation. Key caution: systemic exposure can suppress the adrenal axis; topical overuse can thin skin.
Class: bisphosphonate. Use: osteoporosis. Key caution: esophageal irritation; oral administration requires specific upright and fasting precautions.
Class: bisphosphonate. Use: osteoporosis. Key caution: esophageal injury and rare atypical femoral fractures or jaw osteonecrosis.
Class: xanthine oxidase inhibitor. Use: long-term urate lowering in gout and selected hyperuricemia. Key caution: severe hypersensitivity reactions; major interaction with azathioprine.

Class: microtubule inhibitor with anti-inflammatory effects. Use: gout flares or prophylaxis and selected pericarditis regimens. Key caution: severe toxicity with renal impairment or strong CYP3A/P-glycoprotein inhibitors.
Class: SSRI antidepressant. Use: depression and several anxiety-related disorders. Key caution: serotonin syndrome, discontinuation symptoms and age-related suicidality warning.
Class: SSRI antidepressant. Use: depression and selected anxiety or eating disorders. Key caution: long half-life prolongs interactions; serotonin syndrome with serotonergic combinations.
Class: SSRI antidepressant. Use: depression and generalized anxiety disorder. Key caution: serotonin syndrome and dose-related QT concerns in susceptible patients.
Class: SSRI antidepressant. Use: depression. Key caution: dose-dependent QT prolongation.
Class: SSRI antidepressant. Use: depression and selected anxiety disorders. Key caution: prominent discontinuation symptoms and CYP2D6 interactions.
Class: SNRI antidepressant. Use: depression and selected anxiety disorders. Key caution: increased blood pressure and discontinuation symptoms.
Class: SNRI antidepressant. Use: depression, anxiety and selected chronic pain conditions. Key caution: liver injury risk and serotonergic interactions.

Class: norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor. Use: depression and smoking cessation depending on formulation. Key caution: lowers seizure threshold; contraindicated in seizure and certain eating disorders.
Class: alpha-2 antagonist antidepressant with serotonergic receptor effects. Use: depression. Key caution: sedation and weight gain.
Class: serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor. Use: depression; often used off-label for insomnia. Key caution: sedation, orthostatic hypotension and rare priapism.
Class: tricyclic antidepressant. Use: depression and selected off-label pain conditions. Key caution: anticholinergic effects and dangerous cardiac toxicity in overdose.
Class: tricyclic antidepressant. Use: depression and selected off-label pain conditions. Key caution: conduction abnormalities, anticholinergic effects and overdose toxicity.
Class: serotonin 5-HT1A partial agonist anxiolytic. Use: generalized anxiety. Key caution: delayed benefit; not an immediate rescue medicine or treatment for benzodiazepine withdrawal.
Class: benzodiazepine. Use: selected anxiety and panic disorders. Key caution: dependence, withdrawal and respiratory depression with opioids or other sedatives.
Class: benzodiazepine. Use: anxiety and selected acute seizure or sedation settings. Key caution: sedation, dependence and respiratory depression, especially with opioids.
Class: benzodiazepine. Use: selected seizure disorders and panic disorder. Key caution: dependence and withdrawal seizures with abrupt discontinuation.
Class: benzodiazepine. Use: selected anxiety, muscle spasm, seizures and alcohol withdrawal. Key caution: prolonged sedation and respiratory depression with other depressants.
Class: nonbenzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic. Use: insomnia. Key caution: complex sleep behaviors and next-day impairment.
Class: nonbenzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic. Use: insomnia. Key caution: complex sleep behaviors and next-day impairment.

Class: second-generation antipsychotic. Use: schizophrenia and bipolar disorder; some formulations adjunctively treat depression. Key caution: sedation and metabolic effects; increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis.

Class: second-generation antipsychotic. Use: schizophrenia, bipolar mania and selected behavioral indications. Key caution: prolactin elevation and movement disorders; dementia-related mortality warning.
Class: second-generation antipsychotic. Use: schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Key caution: substantial weight gain and metabolic abnormalities; dementia-related mortality warning.

Class: dopamine D2 partial agonist antipsychotic. Use: schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and adjunctive depression treatment. Key caution: akathisia and impulse-control problems; dementia-related mortality warning.
Class: first-generation antipsychotic. Use: psychotic disorders and selected severe agitation. Key caution: extrapyramidal effects, QT prolongation and neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
Class: mood stabilizer. Use: bipolar disorder. Key caution: narrow therapeutic index; renal impairment, dehydration, NSAIDs and several antihypertensives can increase toxicity.
Class: antiseizure medicine and mood stabilizer. Use: epilepsy and bipolar maintenance. Key caution: serious rash, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, especially with rapid titration.
Class: broad-spectrum antiseizure medicine. Use: epilepsy; related valproate formulations treat bipolar disorder or prevent migraine. Key caution: major fetal harm, hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.
Class: SV2A-binding antiseizure medicine. Use: selected seizure disorders. Key caution: behavioral changes and mood symptoms; renal function affects dosing.
Class: sodium-channel-blocking antiseizure medicine. Use: focal seizures and trigeminal neuralgia. Key caution: serious rash, blood dyscrasias and extensive drug interactions.
Class: sodium-channel-blocking antiseizure medicine. Use: focal seizures. Key caution: hyponatremia and serious skin reactions.
Class: antiseizure medicine with multiple mechanisms. Use: epilepsy and migraine prevention. Key caution: cognitive slowing, kidney stones, metabolic acidosis and fetal risk.

Class: alpha-2-delta calcium-channel ligand. Use: focal-seizure adjunct therapy and postherpetic neuralgia. Key caution: sedation and respiratory depression with opioids; renal adjustment is important.

Class: alpha-2-delta calcium-channel ligand. Use: selected neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia and focal-seizure adjunct therapy. Key caution: sedation, edema and respiratory depression with other depressants.
Class: serotonin 5-HT1B/1D agonist. Use: acute migraine and some cluster-headache formulations. Key caution: vasoconstriction; contraindicated in certain ischemic vascular diseases.
Class: acetylcholinesterase inhibitor. Use: symptomatic treatment of Alzheimer dementia. Key caution: bradycardia, syncope and gastrointestinal effects.
Class: NMDA receptor antagonist. Use: moderate-to-severe Alzheimer dementia. Key caution: dizziness or confusion; renal function affects dosing.
Class: peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor plus dopamine precursor. Use: Parkinson disease motor symptoms. Key caution: dyskinesias, orthostatic hypotension and hallucinations.
Class: dopamine agonist. Use: Parkinson disease and selected restless legs syndrome. Key caution: sudden sleep episodes, impulse-control problems and symptom augmentation in restless legs syndrome.
Class: dopamine agonist. Use: Parkinson disease and selected restless legs syndrome. Key caution: sleep attacks, impulse-control problems and renal accumulation.
Class: central nervous system stimulant. Use: ADHD and selected narcolepsy. Key caution: misuse potential and increases in heart rate or blood pressure.
Class: central nervous system stimulant combination. Use: ADHD and selected narcolepsy. Key caution: misuse, dependence and cardiovascular effects.
Class: prodrug stimulant. Use: ADHD and moderate-to-severe binge-eating disorder in adults. Key caution: misuse potential and cardiovascular effects.
Class: selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor. Use: ADHD. Key caution: suicidal-ideation warning in children and adolescents; rare severe liver injury.
Class: non-opioid analgesic and antipyretic. Use: pain and fever. Key caution: liver toxicity with excessive total intake, including duplicate combination products.
Class: nonselective NSAID. Use: pain, fever and inflammation. Key caution: gastrointestinal bleeding, kidney injury and cardiovascular risk; pregnancy timing matters.
Class: nonselective NSAID. Use: pain and inflammation. Key caution: gastrointestinal bleeding and kidney injury; cardiovascular and pregnancy-related risks remain.
Class: NSAID. Use: osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis symptoms. Key caution: gastrointestinal bleeding, renal injury and cardiovascular events.
Class: COX-2-selective NSAID. Use: arthritis and selected pain conditions. Key caution: cardiovascular and gastrointestinal risks; reduced platelet effects do not make it risk-free.
Class: NSAID. Use: inflammatory or musculoskeletal pain; formulation matters. Key caution: cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, renal and hepatic toxicity, especially with systemic use.
Class: opioid agonist with serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake effects. Use: selected pain. Key caution: respiratory depression, seizures, serotonin syndrome and dependence.
Class: opioid agonist. Use: selected pain and some cough products. Key caution: respiratory depression and dependence; combination products may add acetaminophen toxicity risk.
Class: opioid agonist. Use: pain severe enough to require an opioid. Key caution: potentially fatal respiratory depression and dependence.
Class: opioid agonist. Use: severe pain in selected settings. Key caution: respiratory depression and accumulation of active metabolites with renal dysfunction.

Class: partial mu-opioid agonist. Use: opioid use disorder or pain depending on formulation. Key caution: can precipitate withdrawal when started after other opioids; respiratory risk rises with sedatives.
Class: opioid antagonist. Use: reversal of suspected opioid overdose. Key caution: its effect can wear off before the opioid; recurrent respiratory depression and precipitated withdrawal can occur.
Class: centrally acting skeletal-muscle relaxant. Use: short-term acute musculoskeletal spasm. Key caution: sedation, anticholinergic effects and serotonergic interactions.
Class: central alpha-2 agonist muscle relaxant. Use: spasticity. Key caution: hypotension and major interactions with ciprofloxacin or fluvoxamine.
Class: GABA-B agonist. Use: spasticity. Key caution: abrupt withdrawal, especially intrathecal, can be life-threatening; renal dysfunction increases toxicity.
Class: centrally acting muscle relaxant. Use: short-term musculoskeletal spasm. Key caution: sedation and impaired driving, amplified by other depressants.

Class: aminopenicillin antibiotic. Use: susceptible bacterial infections such as selected ear, respiratory and dental infections. Key caution: serious beta-lactam allergy and antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
Class: aminopenicillin plus beta-lactamase inhibitor. Use: selected susceptible bacterial infections. Key caution: diarrhea and cholestatic liver injury.
Class: natural penicillin antibiotic. Use: susceptible infections such as streptococcal pharyngitis. Key caution: immediate hypersensitivity, including anaphylaxis.

Class: first-generation cephalosporin. Use: selected skin infections and other susceptible bacterial infections. Key caution: allergy and antibiotic-associated diarrhea; renal function affects dosing.
Class: second-generation cephalosporin. Use: selected respiratory and other susceptible infections. Key caution: hypersensitivity and antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
Class: third-generation oral cephalosporin. Use: selected respiratory and other susceptible infections. Key caution: diarrhea; iron products can reduce absorption.

Class: third-generation parenteral cephalosporin. Use: serious susceptible infections and selected gonorrhea regimens. Key caution: neonatal bilirubin displacement and neonatal IV calcium incompatibility.
Class: macrolide antibiotic. Use: selected respiratory infections and certain sexually transmitted infections. Key caution: QT prolongation in susceptible patients.
Class: macrolide antibiotic. Use: selected respiratory infections and combination H. pylori regimens. Key caution: QT prolongation and extensive CYP3A interactions.

Class: tetracycline antibiotic. Use: acne and selected bacterial, tick-borne and other infections. Key caution: esophagitis and photosensitivity; pregnancy and age considerations depend on indication.
Class: tetracycline antibiotic. Use: acne and susceptible infections. Key caution: vestibular effects, pigmentation and rare autoimmune reactions.
Class: lincosamide antibiotic. Use: selected anaerobic and gram-positive infections. Key caution: substantial risk of Clostridioides difficile colitis.
Class: fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Use: selected susceptible infections. Key caution: tendon injury, neuropathy and central nervous system effects; important drug interactions.

Class: fluoroquinolone antibiotic. Use: selected respiratory and urinary infections when appropriate. Key caution: tendon injury, neuropathy, QT prolongation and other potentially serious class effects.
Class: nitroimidazole antimicrobial. Use: selected anaerobic bacterial and protozoal infections. Key caution: neuropathy with prolonged exposure and interaction with warfarin.
Class: sequential folate-pathway inhibitor antibiotic combination. Use: selected urinary, skin and opportunistic infections. Key caution: severe rash, hyperkalemia and interaction with warfarin.
Class: nitrofuran urinary antibacterial. Use: susceptible lower urinary tract infection. Key caution: not appropriate for pyelonephritis; renal function and pulmonary or hepatic toxicity matter.

Class: glycopeptide antibiotic. Use: serious gram-positive infections intravenously; oral treatment targets intestinal C. difficile. Key caution: nephrotoxicity and infusion reactions with systemic use.
Class: triazole antifungal. Use: selected Candida and other fungal infections. Key caution: hepatic injury, QT prolongation and drug interactions.
Class: polyene antifungal. Use: local Candida infections of skin or mucosa. Key caution: local formulations do not treat systemic fungal infection.
Class: allylamine antifungal. Use: dermatophyte infections, including oral therapy for selected nail infections. Key caution: oral therapy can cause liver injury and taste disturbance.
Class: antiviral nucleoside analog. Use: herpes simplex and varicella-zoster infections. Key caution: kidney injury, especially with IV use or dehydration; renal adjustment matters.
Class: acyclovir prodrug antiviral. Use: herpes simplex and varicella-zoster infections. Key caution: renal accumulation can cause kidney or neurologic toxicity.
Class: neuraminidase inhibitor antiviral. Use: influenza treatment or prophylaxis in selected patients. Key caution: nausea and vomiting; renal function affects dosing.
Class: short-acting beta-2 agonist. Use: rapid relief of bronchospasm. Key caution: tachycardia and tremor; frequent need suggests inadequate disease control.
Class: short-acting beta-2 agonist. Use: relief of bronchospasm. Key caution: tachycardia, tremor and paradoxical bronchospasm.

Class: short-acting inhaled muscarinic antagonist. Use: COPD bronchodilation and selected acute asthma combinations. Key caution: eye exposure can worsen narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention may occur.
Class: long-acting inhaled muscarinic antagonist. Use: COPD maintenance and selected asthma add-on treatment. Key caution: not a rescue inhaler; urinary retention and glaucoma precautions.

Class: corticosteroid. Use: asthma control or allergic rhinitis depending on formulation. Key caution: inhaled therapy can cause oral candidiasis; potent CYP3A inhibitors may increase systemic exposure.

Class: corticosteroid. Use: asthma or selected gastrointestinal inflammatory disease depending on formulation. Key caution: local candidiasis with inhaled use and systemic steroid effects with sufficient exposure.
Class: inhaled or intranasal corticosteroid. Use: asthma control or allergic rhinitis depending on product. Key caution: oral candidiasis with inhaled therapy; not for immediate bronchospasm relief.

Class: inhaled corticosteroid plus long-acting beta-2 agonist. Use: maintenance treatment of asthma or COPD depending on product. Key caution: not a rescue medicine; oral candidiasis and beta-agonist effects.

Class: inhaled corticosteroid plus long-acting beta-2 agonist. Use: asthma or COPD maintenance; some asthma regimens also use it as reliever under guideline-based plans. Key caution: regimen and product labeling must be verified; do not assume all combination inhalers are interchangeable.

Class: leukotriene-receptor antagonist. Use: selected asthma and allergic rhinitis management. Key caution: serious neuropsychiatric effects; allergic-rhinitis use is restricted to appropriate alternatives-failed settings.
Class: second-generation H1 antihistamine. Use: allergic rhinitis and urticaria. Key caution: drowsiness can occur; rare severe itching may follow stopping long-term use.
Class: second-generation H1 antihistamine. Use: allergic rhinitis and urticaria. Key caution: hepatic or renal impairment may alter dosing needs.
Class: second-generation H1 antihistamine. Use: allergic rhinitis and urticaria. Key caution: fruit juices and aluminum- or magnesium-containing antacids can reduce absorption.
Class: first-generation H1 antihistamine. Use: selected allergic symptoms. Key caution: sedation and anticholinergic toxicity, especially in older adults.
Class: first-generation H1 antihistamine. Use: itching and selected anxiety symptoms. Key caution: sedation, anticholinergic effects and QT prolongation.
Class: proton-pump inhibitor. Use: acid reflux and ulcer-related conditions. Key caution: interaction with clopidogrel and potential complications of unnecessary long-term acid suppression.
Class: proton-pump inhibitor. Use: acid reflux and erosive esophagitis. Key caution: acute interstitial nephritis and low magnesium can occur.
Class: proton-pump inhibitor. Use: acid reflux and selected ulcer-prevention regimens. Key caution: interactions, including with clopidogrel, and adverse effects with prolonged use.
Class: proton-pump inhibitor. Use: acid-related disorders. Key caution: acute interstitial nephritis and increased risk of some enteric infections.
Class: H2-receptor antagonist. Use: acid reflux and peptic ulcer disease. Key caution: renal accumulation may increase confusion or other adverse effects.
Class: mucosal protective agent. Use: duodenal ulcers. Key caution: binds other medicines and reduces absorption; aluminum accumulation is a concern in severe renal disease.
Class: serotonin 5-HT3 antagonist. Use: prevention or treatment of selected nausea and vomiting. Key caution: QT prolongation, especially with electrolyte abnormalities or interacting drugs.
Class: sedating H1 antihistamine with antiemetic effects. Use: selected nausea and allergic conditions. Key caution: respiratory depression; contraindicated in children younger than two years.
Class: dopamine antagonist and prokinetic. Use: selected gastroparesis and short-term reflux treatment. Key caution: tardive dyskinesia, especially with prolonged use.

Class: peripheral opioid-receptor agonist antidiarrheal. Use: selected noninvasive diarrhea. Key caution: excessive doses can cause fatal arrhythmias; avoid in certain inflammatory or infectious diarrheas.
Class: osmotic laxative. Use: constipation. Key caution: suspected bowel obstruction requires evaluation rather than laxative use.
Class: osmotic laxative and ammonia-lowering agent. Use: constipation and hepatic encephalopathy. Key caution: excessive diarrhea can cause dehydration and electrolyte disturbances.
Class: stimulant laxative. Use: constipation. Key caution: cramping and electrolyte loss with excessive use.
Class: stool softener surfactant. Use: selected constipation situations. Key caution: evidence of benefit is limited; avoid with suspected bowel obstruction.
Class: alpha-1A-preferring antagonist. Use: lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic enlargement. Key caution: orthostatic symptoms and intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.

Class: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor. Use: benign prostatic enlargement or male-pattern hair loss depending on strength. Key caution: fetal risk from exposure in pregnancy; lowers PSA and complicates interpretation.
Class: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor. Use: benign prostatic enlargement. Key caution: fetal risk and reduction of PSA values.
Class: phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor. Use: erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension depending on product. Key caution: severe hypotension with nitrates.

Class: phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor. Use: erectile dysfunction, benign prostatic enlargement or pulmonary arterial hypertension depending on product. Key caution: nitrate interaction persists because of its long duration.
Class: antimuscarinic. Use: overactive bladder. Key caution: dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention and cognitive adverse effects.
Class: antimuscarinic. Use: overactive bladder. Key caution: urinary retention, anticholinergic effects and QT concerns in susceptible patients.
Class: beta-3 adrenergic agonist. Use: overactive bladder. Key caution: can raise blood pressure and inhibit CYP2D6, affecting other drugs.
Class: oral iron replacement. Use: iron deficiency. Key caution: gastrointestinal effects and potentially fatal poisoning in children after overdose.
Class: electrolyte replacement. Use: potassium deficiency. Key caution: hyperkalemia and arrhythmias, especially with kidney disease or potassium-retaining drugs.
Class: vitamin B9 replacement. Use: folate deficiency and selected pregnancy-related supplementation. Key caution: can improve anemia while masking untreated vitamin B12 deficiency.
Class: vitamin B12 replacement. Use: vitamin B12 deficiency. Key caution: route and duration depend on the cause; neurologic injury may persist if treatment is delayed.
